accepted_review_findings:
[reviewer finding R2-1, low] The authoritative platform describes cpu_python_execution only as running a script by relative path. It does not describe passing command-line arguments. task.md nevertheless tells the solver to run the copied checker 'with the argument results/proposal.json'. The public checker docstring shows a shell command line, but no shell exists. The checker's 'proposal' positional argument is required. If the tool cannot pass arguments, a solver following the instructions literally gets an argparse error (exit 2). The optional helper then fails as documented unless the solver writes its own wrapper. The deliverable contract itself is unaffected, so the impact is small, but this is a repairable contract inaccuracy under the v7 platform check. It was not raised in the previous review.
Required repair: In check_proposal.py, make the positional argument optional with a default: ap.add_argument('proposal', nargs='?', default='results/proposal.json'). Rewrite the docstring usage as 'write a copy into /work (e.g. tools/check_proposal.py) and run the copy with cpu_python_execution; by default it checks results/proposal.json'. Remove the shell command line. In task.md Section 5 step 2, replace 'Run the copy with the argument results/proposal.json' with 'Run the copy with cpu_python_execution; it checks results/proposal.json by default'. environment/smoke.py calls mod.main([doc_path, ...]) explicitly and keeps working unchanged. Re-hash the two assets.
controller_notes: [controller note] Authoritative signature of the platform CPU tool (runtime interface v4): cpu.run(script: relative .py artifact path under /work, arguments: optional list[str], timeout_seconds: optional positive number clipped to the remaining package wall time). It returns returncode/stdout/stderr/timed_out/output_limited. Public assets are mounted read-only at /inputs/public/<path>; a public script must first be copied into /work with the artifact tools before cpu.run can execute it. Describe running the checker exactly in these terms (passing command-line arguments through the arguments list is supported).
